eli5.text: When you start the coding helper, it no longer prints three lines of startup text saying it's ready and waiting for your first command. Those messages were removed so the helper starts up faster and with less noise before showing you its main prompt.

ai.title: Filter large low-priority files in prompt context
ai.summary: updateFileContext in backend/src/main-prompt.ts now filters loaded files before building prompt context. Files ranked beyond the top 5 are excluded if countTokens exceeds 5,000. This prevents oversized, low-priority files from consuming the context window.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to work on a task, it pulls in relevant files to understand your project. Now, if your project has a lot of files, the system automatically leaves out the extra-large ones that aren't the most important, so it can focus on the key files first. This keeps the conversation sharper and avoids getting bogged down by huge, less important files. If you use the assistant today, you'd notice it's better at picking the most relevant files to read upfront.

ai.title: Truncate git changes, bump file tree budget to 80k
ai.summary: Adds `truncateString` and `countTokensJson` to prevent oversized prompts. `getGitChangesPrompt` now truncates diffs and status to 30k chars (10% for status/commits). `getProjectFileTreePrompt` budget increases from 60k to 80k tokens. Token counting shifts to JSON-stringified length for accuracy.

eli5.text: When the assistant looks at your project's recent changes or its file structure, it now keeps those descriptions shorter so they fit within a size limit, and it counts how much text there is more accurately. You will notice that details about your files and recent edits are summarized instead of shown in full when there is a lot of them, and the assistant gets a bigger allowance (80,000 units) to describe your project's file layout. The change is live today.

ai.title: Bump manicode package version to 1.0.76
ai.summary: Version increment in `npm-app/package.json` from 1.0.75 to 1.0.76. Internal release marker for the `manicode` package.

eli5.text: Internal tooling that builds and ships the assistant program advanced to a new release number today. If you look at your installation, it will now report a newer version than before; otherwise nothing visible changes in how it feels to run it. This is housekeeping that keeps automated updates and dependencies moving forward.

ai.title: Unify project root and working directory in CLI
ai.summary: Project root is now the current directory. `setProjectRoot` replaces `initProjectRoot` and prints a green message when the directory changes. `getCurrentWorkingDirectory` and `setCurrentWorkingDirectory` are removed in favor of `getProjectRoot`. Terminal commands and file contexts use `getProjectRoot` directly.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, it now treats wherever you launched it from as your project folder, instead of tracking a separate 'project folder' and 'current working directory' behind the scenes. If you tell the assistant to switch to a different folder (for example, by running 'cd some/other/folder'), it will move there and print a short green confirmation so you can see that file reads and writes have moved to that new location. The prompt you type at still shows the name of the current folder, but it's now reading from the single, unified project folder rather than a previously separate working directory.

ai.title: /run prefix added to CLI terminal command detection
ai.summary: CLI now recognizes `/run <command>` prefix for terminal execution. Detection logic allows up to 5 tokens (previously <4) without prefix. Menu help text updated to document `/run` usage. Internal change in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` and `npm-app/src/menu.ts`.

eli5.text: When you type a command in the assistant's chat, it now recognizes when you start with "/run" to explicitly tell it to run a terminal command, instead of the system having to guess from the words alone. The assistant also gives a bit more leeway in guessing short commands that look like they're meant for the terminal, allowing up to five words instead of fewer, even without the "/run" prefix. These updates are live today, so the changes are effective now.

ai.title: Version 1.0.77
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.77 in npm-app/package.json. Reflects minor release progression. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The assistant you use just got bumped to version 1.0.77. This update lets the command line tool now recognize a `/run` prefix when you type terminal commands, so commands like `/run build` will execute correctly. It also unifies the project root with the current working directory, so the assistant will more reliably operate in the folder you're actually working in. These changes are live today.
